Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: E01, a bespoke CONTINUOUS TRANSITION ENVIRONMENT PAINTING from Wound Slope to Baleen Filter, original 2D side-scrolling adventure inside a colossal DEAD baleen whale. Reference1 is the departure room, reference2 is arrival. Paint a NEW unified composition that reconstructs their connecting area. Do not paste, mirror, stretch, or place two rectangular pictures side by side.
Wide 2.4:1 landscape side elevation, one connected scene with NO panel line or visible seam. Left quarter is the END of the first room: descending dusty-rose fleshy road beyond its central arch, under a relatively sparse ivory upper-jaw baleen fringe. Central half is the passage: broad WALKABLE unbroken nearly level gentle lower-jaw edge, substantial ivory porous ROOT SUPPORT under its rose skin, sweeping huge DIAGONAL JAW BONE behind and above the path. Right quarter is the START of filter room: the same floor rolls into its first low mound; dense pale baleen curtains become progressively longer overhead. A few high LEFT wall-rooted old-wound shelves may be glimpsed far in arrival background, but do not create a new side route in this connection.
The diagonal jaw arch must pass smoothly across left, center and right as ONE landmark in medium distance. Far blue water and immense opposite jaw structures match across the full width. All playable path silhouettes stay at similar lower-frame height; no dangerous gap, doorway, barrier, rope bridge or new puzzle. Platforms and bone support look organically grown from the body, not pasted thin slabs or repeating triangles. No enemies or collectibles in this connector, no new shelter or altar. One TINY original diver for scale near left road: rounded ivory head with one round dark lens, teal short cape, U-shaped two-prong resonator, tiny amber sealed hip lamp, red tether.
Maintain source painting style: detailed matte gouache, wet muted rose tissue, grey-ivory calcareous bone, dark blue underwater depth, restrained amber ecological tips, sparse distant small fish and a few bubbles, no flame. Foreground dark softly blurred shell roots at bottom corners, never across foot surfaces. Dense ecological growth at attachments, large quiet water negative spaces. No tile wallpaper, masonry, insect civilization, knight/horns, sword/nail, text, arrows, labels, numbers, diagrams or borders. Strong original whale anatomy, playable route readable. This is a single transitional space, not a whole new room.
